title: Contract checks for tool-call compatibility during progressive rollouts
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Introduce a lightweight contract/compatibility checker that runs during canary, A/B, and shadow rollouts to detect tool-calling and structured-output incompatibilities between the baseline model and candidate variants. The goal is to surface regressions early (function signature changes, missing required fields, type mismatches, or semantic shape shifts) and feed automatic rollback or traffic-scaling rules. This ticket scopes the rollout-side comparator, the canonicalization rules, comparator metrics, and integration points with the Console's rollout UI and Auto-Rollback engine.
background: We have observed subtle breakages where new model variants change function-call payload shapes (optional -> required, enum renames), or emit extra wrapper fields that downstream tool runners don't expect. Existing heuristics (exact JSON equality) are too brittle and produce false-positives for reordered keys, minor formatting, or added benign fields. Prior work (ENG-4821, ENG-7392) covered gating and schema guards but did not provide a rollout-time comparator that: 1) compares effective contract equivalence, 2) quantifies risk with a compact metric, and 3) can run at sampling rates consistent with canaries and A/B traffic.
proposed_solution: Build a comparator service that consumes paired outputs from baseline and candidate during shadow/canary traffic. Steps: 1) canonicalize both outputs (stable key ordering, remove tracing metadata, normalize timestamps), 2) apply a configurable schema overlay (OpenAPI/JSON-Schema or function signature template) to identify required fields and types, 3) compute a set of diffs: missing required fields, type mismatches, enum/constant drift, extra top-level keys, and function-call arg count changes, 4) score diffs into a 'contract-distance' (0.0-1.0) with weighted buckets for severity, 5) emit real-time metrics and histogram summaries into Console; feed thresholds into the Auto-Rollback controller. Comparator must support streaming partial outputs (for streaming function-calls) and tolerant matching for reordered arrays when annotated with a 'set' hint.
tradeoffs_and_considerations: Exact-JSON equality is low-cost but high-false-positive; our comparator increases CPU work during rollouts — we will sample at 5-20% by default.
Tight type checking reduces regression risk but can block backward-compatible extensions; we allow 'opt-in strictness' per route/model via rollout policy.
Canonicalization rules must be conservative to avoid masking real regressions (e.g., don't drop user-visible wrapper fields).
implementation_notes: Use existing streaming capture layer to fork requests to comparator via shadow stream — add lightweight protobuf envelope for paired records.
Leverage existing JSON-Schema library but extend with function-call-aware checks (positional vs named args, variadic allowances).
Add config in rollout manifest: sample_rate, strictness_level (lenient|default|strict), severity_weights, auto_rollback_threshold.
Comparator will publish Prometheus metrics: contract_distance_avg, contract_distance_p95, missing_required_field_rate, func_arg_count_diff_rate.
Create a 'diff preview' artifact saved to S3 for any paired trace that exceeds a threshold — Console will render these diffs for PM/Design review.
Performance target: comparator latency <= 30ms p95 on sampled requests; CPU overhead <= 8% on dedicated canary nodes.
Edge cases: streaming partial function-calls — buffer up to 256 tokens or 100ms to allow stable parsing; if incomplete, mark as 'partial' and exclude from auto-rollback metrics unless repeated.
Security: comparator will redact PII and secrets using existing redact pipeline before persistence.
Fail-open behavior: comparator unavailability must not affect live traffic — shadowing is async and non-blocking.
acceptance_criteria: Comparator ingests paired baseline+candidate outputs for shadowed requests and emits contract_distance metric.
Console shows a histogram and top 10 diff types for each rollout and ability to drill into individual diff preview artifacts.
Auto-Rollback controller can be configured to trigger if contract_distance_p95 > 0.35 for 10 minutes or missing_required_field_rate > 0.01 for the same window.
Sampling defaults implemented (5%) and adjustable per-rollout manifest.
Comparator supports streaming function-call diffs and marks partial streams appropriately.
Unit and e2e tests cover canonicalization, JSON-Schema overlays, and scoring weights with synthetic examples.
Benchmark shows comparator p95 latency <= 30ms and CPU overhead within acceptable limits on canary hardware profiles.
Docs updated: rollout contract checks guide, Console screenshots, and example rollout manifest.
Security review completed and redaction validated (if security_review_required == true this flag would be set).
Design review (Design owner) approved the Console render for diff previews and the UX for 'preview then rollback'.
